TITLE: Comparing Symplectic Integrators for RNN Stability
PROPOSAL: Explore the effectiveness of symplectic integrators (e.g., RK4, Dopri5) in addressing vanishing gradients in discrete RNNs on a collection of temporal benchmark tasks generated using a probabilistic physics simulator (e.g., Probabilistic Physics Engine). Train and evaluate model performance on metrics such as accuracy, generalized energy conservation, and structure-preserving properties using datasets with simple, invertible dynamics.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Traditional LSTM counterpart on the same tasks; Ablation: Key error correction mechanisms (e.g., tanh, softmax) disabled to understand their role in stability enhancement.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected to see a significant reduction in vanishing gradient effects and improvement in accuracy compared to LSTM, with possible variations in performance across tasks due to symplectic integrator choices and model architectures. Stability might degrade with increased task complexity or dynamics non-invertibility.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Hamiltonian Neural Networks on Higher-Dimensional Datasets
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of Hamiltonian Neural Networks (HNNs) on a variety of high-dimensional synthetic datasets sampling physical systems under various energy constraints, such as simulated chemical reactions, thermalization processes, or many-body interactions. Evaluate model efficiency, conservation properties, and parameterized generalizability with respect to system complexity and primary variables. Compare against discrete RNNs and continuous Neural ODEs on equivalent datasets and metrics.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Neural ODEs and standard RNNs; Ablation: Role of the symplectic form and imposed constraints in the HNN; Compare benefits in preserving information while scaling up in dimensionality.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: HNNs should perform better than traditional ODEs in retaining information over long horizons, and comparable to high-dimensional RNNs with symplectic constraints. Their performance may degrade for highly non-linear or dissipative dynamics. The quality of the symplectic form may significantly impact model efficacy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Physical Invariance in Neural Network Training
PROPOSAL: Examine the effect of incorporating invariants derived from physical laws and symmetries (e.g., Hamiltonian conservation, angular momentum) directly into the loss or normalizer functions of RNNs, ODEs, and HNNs, using theoretically generated or physically-simulated (PS) datasets. Compare model performance against a baseline lacking these invariants and assess their impact on generalization and interpretability across model types.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Model without invariance term; Ablation: Impact of including conserved quantities vs derived constraints on convergence speed, fit quality and Vapnik-Chervonenkis VC-dimension.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected to see improvements in accuracy and a significant reduction in overfitting for models incorporating physical invariants, particularly for dynamical systems governed by classical mechanics. The effect might be less pronounced for systems where invariants are not explicitly conserved.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Long-Term Stability Analysis of Hybrid Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: Develop a deep learning framework that integrates elements of both discrete and continuous-time representations to construct hybrid neural networks that can model long-term dynamics of physical systems. This will involve the combination of Hamiltonian neural networks with continuous-time representations, such as Neural ODEs, and discrete-time models, such as Symplectic RNNs. Investigate the long-term stability of these hybrid networks using Lyapunov functions and other metrics.

CONTROLS: Compare the performance of hybrid networks with different component architectures and integration methods; investigate the effect of dimensionality and complexity on long-term stability. Baseline models will include isolated continuous-time or discrete-time models.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This hybrid approach is expected to provide a flexible and stable framework for modeling long-term physical dynamics, combining the benefits of continuous-time and discrete-time representations. The resulting model is likely to have improved long-term stability and generalization capabilities compared to traditional RNNs or continuous-time models alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Validation of Deep Learning Models for Physical Systems
PROPOSAL: Design and execute an experimental validation framework for the proposed deep learning models (Comparing Symplectic Integrators for RNN Stability, Evaluating Hamiltonian Neural Networks on Higher-Dimensional Datasets, Investigating the Role of Physical Invariance in Neural Network Training, Quantum Mechanical Operator-Learned Hamiltonian Dynamics, Universal Conserved Quantities for Temporally Steady Networks, and Long-Term Stability Analysis of Hybrid Neural Networks) on a range of physical systems and tasks. This will involve collecting and processing experimental data from real-world experiments, as well as comparing the performance of the deep learning models to classical and traditional methods.

CONTROLS: Compare the performance of deep learning models against a variety of baselines, including classical methods and state-of-the-art machine learning models; investigate the robustness and generalizability of the deep learning models across different physical systems and experimental conditions.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This experimental validation framework is expected to provide a rigorous test of the proposed deep learning models and provide insights into their potential to model and simulate complex physical systems. The results will help identify the strengths and limitations of the deep learning models and guide further development and refinement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conserved Hamiltonian Neural Networks for Temporal Learning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the efficacy of a novel neural network architecture that combines the principles of Hamiltonian mechanics with Neural ODEs to enforce energy conservation and symplectic structure in temporal learning. This architecture will leverage the conserved quantities of Hamiltonian systems to regularize the learning process, ensure stability, and preserve information over long timescales.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard Neural ODEs and Hamiltonian Neural Networks on tasks such as predictive modeling of chaotic systems and long-term forecasting in synthetic datasets like Lorenz-96.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect significant improvements in stability and long-term performance on synthetic tasks, but potential difficulties in generalizing to high-dimensional real-world data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Symplectic Transformers for Energy-Preserving Temporal Learning
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel variant of the Transformer architecture, specifically designed to incorporate symplectic structure and energy conservation principles. This Symplectic Transformer will utilize mixed-precision arithmetic to approximate symplectic flows, and a specially designed energy penalty term to prevent the destruction of information over time.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard Transformer models on tasks such as predictive modeling and long-term sequence forecasting using energy-preserving datasets like the RVT-MAR drifting pendulum simulation.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the Symplectic Transformer to outperform standard Transformers on energy-preserving tasks, but possible loss of generality due to the specifically designed energy penalty term, which might need to be re-tuned for each new scenario.

TITLE: Conserved Hamiltonian Neural Networks for Temporal Learning
PROPOSAL: Refine the initial proposal of Conserved Hamiltonian Neural Networks (CHNNs) by incorporating a new component: a.Registry - an internal learned representation of the symplectic structure, serving as a meta-kernel that computes the derivatives and conserved quantities. This enhanced version of CHNNs will be designed to learn symplectic structure in an end-to-end manner, ensuring stability and energy conservation.

TITLE: A Lyapunov Regularized Continuous RNN Architecture
PROPOSAL: Design a novel Lyapunov-Regularized Continuous Recurrent Neural Network (LRC-RNN) that combines the advantages of both continuous-depth models like Neural ODEs and traditional RNNs. The key innovation is the incorporation of a learned Lyapunov function to control the flow of information, thereby ensuring stability and preventing the loss of information over time. This will be demonstrated through experiments on synthetic datasets and long-term forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard RNN models, Neural ODEs, and existing Lyapunov-regularized RNNs to demonstrate the LRC-RNN's superiority in preserving information and maintaining stability on tasks such as Lorenz-96 and other chaotic systems.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the LRC-RNN to outperform traditional RNNs and Neural ODEs by effectively controlling the flow of information and enforcing Lyapunov stability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Physics-Informed Neural PSO for Preserving Energy in Temporal Learning
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel optimization framework for training temporal neural networks, named Physics-Informed Neural Particle Swarm Optimization (PINPSO). This approach incorporates physical constraints and prior knowledge about the underlying dynamical system into the optimization process using ensemble methods and lineage-aware regularization to ensure energy conservation and stable long-term behavior.
CONTROLS: Validate PINPSO on tasks like trajectory prediction, long-term forecasting, and unbalanced dynamics with unstable attractors in synthetic datasets such as those modeled by the logistic map or Kuramoto's oscillator equations.
COST: 420 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the PINPSO approach to outperform standard optimization methods by effectively preserving energy and preventing information loss, but potential limitations arise from the computational complexity of integrating prior knowledge into the training process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning-Driven Time Reversibility for Preserving Information in Temporal Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel method for achieving time-reversibility in temporal neural networks, which is a fundamental concept for preserving information in dynamical systems. This is achieved by introducing a time-reversibility penalty term into the loss function, which encourages the network to learn a symmetric flow with respect to time. We will demonstrate its effectiveness on tasks such as predictive modeling and long-term action recognition.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard temporal neural networks and state-of-the-art methods for enforcing time-reversibility, such as the Symplectic Convolutional Network.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect this approach to improve the preservation of information and temporal coherence in long-term predictions, but may face difficulties in achieving good performance on tasks with non-symmetric dynamics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamic Energy Landscape for Long-Term Stability and Consistency in Temporal Models
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel contrastive learning framework, called Dynamic Energy Landscape (DEL), designed to train temporal neural networks to maintain stability and consistency over long timescales. DEL is based on a dynamic energy landscape that mimics the natural process of energy relaxation in physical systems and encourages temporal models to learn a consistent set of long-term predictions.
CONTROLS: Evaluate DEL against standard temporal models and existing methods for training models with long-term consistency, such as the Temporal Memory Network.
COST: 240 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect DEL to effectively promote stability and consistency in temporal models and significantly outperform existing methods on tasks that require such properties. However, its training may require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Robust Temporal Learning that Preserves Information over Long Horizons
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel adversarial training method for temporal neural networks that adversarially introduces perturbations and evaluates the model's ability to preserve information over long horizons. This approach, called Robust Temporal Learning (RTL), will be used to train temporal models to be robust against perturbations and maintain their performance on tasks that require long-term consistency and stability.
CONTROLS: Validate RTL against existing methods for training robust temporal models, such as the Robust Recurrent Neural Network, on tasks involving long-term predictions and consistency in synthetic datasets.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect RTL to outperform standard adversarial training methods in preserving information over long horizons and achieving robustness against perturbations. However, potential high computational cost may arise from the necessity of frequent adversarial attacks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation and Comparison of Temporal Learning Architectures on a General Benchmark Suite
PROPOSAL: Develop a standardized benchmark suite for evaluating and comparing the performance of various temporal learning architectures on tasks that emphasize long-term information preservation, stability, and robustness. This benchmark suite will be used to compare and analyze the strengths and weaknesses of the architectures proposed in this set, including their capabilities for handling different types of temporal dependencies, and their robustness against noise, perturbations, and other forms of degradation.
CONTROLS: Utilize the proposed architectures from the benchmark suite to demonstrate their effectiveness and, subsequently, to identify areas where future improvements are needed.
COST: 360 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the benchmark suite to significantly aid in understanding the relative merits of each architecture and to provide guidance for future development of temporal learning models that prioritize long-term information preservation, stability, and robustness.

This framework will leverage the Registry component from the revised Conserved Hamiltonian Neural Networks and the adversarial training method from Adversarial Training for Robust Temporal Learning.
CONTROLS: Compare against existing state-of-the-art models on tasks that emphasize long-term information preservation, stability, and robustness, and evaluate the unified framework's ability to adapt to different types of temporal dependencies.

PREDICTION: We anticipate that the unified framework will achieve superior performance and generalizability on tasks requiring long-term information preservation, stability, and robustness, and will serve as a foundation for the development of future temporal learning models.

title: understanding the dissipative nature of neural ode dynamics
PROPOSAL: Investigate the behavior of Neural ODEs in dissipative systems using the Lorenz attractor and compare to a more conservative alternative such as the symplectic Liouville equation. This will provide insight into the dynamics of Neural ODEs and how it compares to more traditional conservative systems.
CONTROLS: Train Neural ODEs on the Lorenz attractor dataset and compare to the symplectic Liouville equation and the original Lorenz system equations.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Neural ODEs should demonstrate dissipative behavior on this conservative system, potentially exhibiting an incomplete preservation of information over time. The inclusion of a symplectic Liouville equation will theoretically maintain information at all times. This comparative study may uncover limitations with Neural ODEs for modeling systems that preserve information over long periods. Failure may arise from the potential emergence of numerical instability in the numerical solution of the ODEs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: exploring the interplay between lyapunov exponents and neural ode stability
PROPOSAL: Investigate the relationship between Lyapunov exponents and Neural ODE stability in various dissipative systems. Introduce a novel Lyapunov regularization term for Neural ODEs and demonstrate its effect on preserving information over time.
CONTROLS: Compare Lyapunov-regularized Neural ODEs to standard Neural ODEs with and without additional regularization terms (e.g., energy-based regularization) on the Henon-Heiles dataset, which demonstrates complex nonlinear dynamics and dissipative behavior.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The introduction of a Lyapunov regularization term for Neural ODEs should improve stability and information preservation over time, but may not reach ideal Lyapunov stability (characterized by vanishing Lyapunov exponents) in all regimes. Incorporating energy-based regularization may improve results but may also hinder performance, especially in dissipative systems where information is lost over time.

This will enable Neural ODEs to more effectively adapt to varying levels of dynamical complexity.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of Adaptive Neural ODEs on the same Henon-Heiles dataset, comparing to standard Neural ODEs and Energy-regularized Neural ODEs. As a more theoretical control, examine the minimal time step required to achieve convergence for various Lyapunov exponents.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Adaptive Neural ODEs should achieve improved information preservation over time, adapting their step size to match the local Lyapunov exponents of the underlying system. This may come at the cost of increased computational expense, and failure may arise if the adaptive scheme does not capture important Lyapunov features or gets stuck in a suboptimal time-stepping regime.

title: hamiltonian neural networks for symplectic integrators

By enforcing the Hamiltonian structure of the system, HNNs should preserve the symplectic form and thus maintain information over time.
CONTROLS: Train HNNs on the Lorenz attractor dataset, comparing performance to standard Neural ODEs and Energy-regularized Neural ODEs. As a theoretical control, analyze the preservation of energy and symplectic form under the Hamiltonian Neural Network.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: HNNs should demonstrate long-term information preservation and symplectic invariance, but computational expense may be high due to the need for symplectic integration; failure may arise from the intrinsic dissipative nature of the Lorenz attractor, which could render the Hamiltonian structure ineffective.
